_note: Drives the Recipe Graph editor. The tool reads this file to build its creatable-vertex palette, the inspector fields for a selected vertex/edge, the legal wiring matrix, and the invariant list it checks after every mutation — nothing about the node kinds is hardcoded in TypeScript beyond the field-type primitives. Adding a vertex kind or a property is a data edit here, not a code change. Map data files (burger.json, ...) are validated against this.

fieldTypes.note: name of another vertex; refKinds restricts which
slot is rendered as a dropdown of the source tool's slotConfig names

mapFields.name: id
mapFields.description: Stable map id, matches the runtime map folder (e.g. "burger").

mapFields.name: gridWidth
mapFields.description: Prep-grid columns. Fixed for every level in the map.

mapFields.name: dirtyStackHeight
mapFields.description: Fallback stack capacity for dirty nodes whose maxStack is blank.

mapFields.name: visibleRows
mapFields.description: Queue rows shown in Play: 1 interactable front row plus previews.

mapFields.name: customerAvatars
mapFields.description: Bundled avatar paths (relative to src/assets/) Play mode draws behind each customer card; one is picked at random per customer.

mapFields.name: idTable
mapFields.description: The five id spaces (ingredient, composite, group, tool, dirty), each an ORDERED list. A row's INDEX is the number level data carries: idTable.ingredient[13] is what a queue digit 13 picks up, and idTable.composite[0] is what a dish's {c0: names. There is no stored id field — the position is the id. Reordering a space therefore renumbers it and re-aims every level string that indexed into it; the editor confirms first. A row is { node } or, once retired, { node: null, retired } — retired rows are kept in place so later rows never shift.

_idTableNote: Sits beside `map` in a map document, NOT inside it — see nodeIdTable.ts. Every integer in a queue, grid or customer string is a DATA ID resolved through this table to a node name; level data never references graph structure. Five spaces (ingredient/composite/group/tool/dirty) because the bracketed dish format names composites and groups by id too ({c0:...} and {g0:...}). Three rules keep committed levels safe as the graph changes: ids are APPEND-ONLY and never reused; deleting a node TOMBSTONES its entry (node: null, old name in `retired`) so a stale reference is a loud error rather than a silent repoint; renaming touches only the `node` field, so the id — and every level using it — is unaffected.

idTableEntryFields.name: id
idTableEntryFields.description: The number that appears in level strings. Assign-once, never reused.

idTableEntryFields.name: node
idTableEntryFields.description: Vertex name this id resolves to. Absent/null marks a tombstone.

idTableEntryFields.name: retired
idTableEntryFields.description: The name this id used to point at. Set together with a null `node`, for diagnostics.

vertexKinds.label: Ingredient
vertexKinds.description: Any concrete item that can sit in a queue, on the prep grid, or in a dish. A pickupable ingredient is a graph leaf; everything else must be produced by exactly one process edge.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Graph-unique key. Referenced by every edge.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: Shown to designers and players.

fields.name: pickupable
fields.description: Comes off the ingredient queue. Marks this vertex as a graph leaf — a traceback terminates here.

fields.name: usageNum
fields.description: How many dish slots ONE landed piece can fill before it is consumed. >1 is a shared sauce (chili bowl 2, cheese sauce 3). Note >1 also disables the skip-the-grid direct-serve path in the runtime.

fields.name: price
fields.description: Economy value from the ingredient table.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Unity-facing string id.

fields.name: emoji
fields.description: Fallback glyph when no artwork resolves.

fields.name: localImage
fields.description: Bundled asset path relative to src/assets/.

fields.name: imageURL
fields.description: Direct web image URL, used after localImage and before fileId.

fields.name: fileId
fields.description: Google Drive artwork id.

vertexKinds.label: Tool
vertexKinds.description: A cooking station. Holds numSlots items at once; each finishes after cookingTime seconds. Owns no recipe data itself — each recipe is one outgoing process edge.

fields.name: slotConfigs
fields.description: The tool's slot POINTS. Each is a named place an ingredient goes, with `slot` parallel positions (lanes). A single-input tool has one point whose `slot` is the old numSlots. A multi-input tool has one point per ingredient - a coffee machine holds ground coffee in one and a cup in another, and brews only once both are filled.

fields.name: cookingTime
fields.description: Default seconds per item; a process edge may override it.

fields.name: upgradeCosts
fields.description: Coin cost per upgrade step, indexed from level 1.

fields.name: imageURL
fields.description: Direct web image URL, used after localImage and before fileId.

vertexKinds.label: Choice group
vertexKinds.description: A reusable choice set referenced as a composite's base or topping, or nested as another group's option. A group always picks a multiset; `maxQuantity` is the only knob. There is deliberately no SINGLE kind — 'exactly one' is maxQuantity 1, which removes a whole class of 'which rule wins' questions.

fields.name: minQuantity
fields.description: Minimum total picks required across all options. Customer strings below this minimum are invalid.

fields.name: maxQuantity
fields.description: Total picks allowed across all options. -1 = unlimited (which makes the enclosing orderable's variant count unbounded — see the resolver); 1 = the old SINGLE, exactly one option chosen.

vertexKinds.label: Composite
vertexKinds.description: A base plus an optional topping — the assembled thing a customer receives. A composite may itself be another composite's base, so assemblies nest.

fields.name: orderable
fields.description: A customer may order this. Marks a graph root — the tracer starts here.

fields.name: toppingRequired
fields.description: The topping slot must be filled. False = a bare base is a legal order (plain fries). Checked when a designer authors a dish and honoured by the customer auto-generator, which fills the slot rather than leaving it empty.

vertexKinds.label: Dirty object
vertexKinds.description: Left on the prep grid when a customer holding the linked composite leaves. Absent = the map's generic dirty dish.

fields.name: maxStack
fields.description: Maximum number of this dirty object in one grid-cell stack. Leave blank to use the map dirtyStackHeight fallback.

fields.name: imageURL
fields.description: Direct web image URL, used after localImage and before fileId.

edgeKinds.label: Processes into
edgeKinds.description: One recipe row: the tool turns `inputs` into the target ingredient. The single most important edge — INV-UNIQUE-PRODUCER caps it at one per target, which is what makes a backward trace deterministic.

fields.name: inputs
fields.description: Ingredients consumed, each with the tool slot POINT it goes into. `slot` indexes the source tool's slotConfigs. Every point named here must be filled before the recipe runs.

fields.name: amount
fields.description: Pieces produced per pickup. A chopping board yielding 2 drops two pieces on the grid at once.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: Overrides the tool's cookingTime for this recipe only.

fields.name: chainTools
fields.description: Extra tools visited in order after the source tool, before the output appears. Produces NO intermediate item and never touches the grid (potato: cutting board, then fryer, then 2 fries).

edgeKinds.label: Base is
edgeKinds.description: What the assembly is built on. Must be present in the dish before any topping can be served onto it.

edgeKinds.label: Topping is
edgeKinds.description: What may go on the base. Optional — a composite with no topping edge is just its base.

edgeKinds.label: Option
edgeKinds.description: One choice within a group. Nesting a group inside a group is legal but must stay acyclic.

fields.name: maxQuantity
fields.description: Max copies of THIS option, independent of the group total. -1 = unlimited. A group capped at 3 whose cheese option is capped at 1 allows three toppings but only one of them cheese.

edgeKinds.label: Leaves behind
edgeKinds.description: The dirty object a served customer leaves. Omit for the map's generic dirty dish.

invariants.description: Every edge endpoint and every ref field names a vertex declared in the same map.
Within an id space, no two rows name the same node. Duplicate IDS are impossible by construction — an id is an array index.
Every non-tombstone id-table entry names a vertex that exists and is of that space's kind.
No level string references a tombstoned id. Checked against the level dataset, so deleting a node that levels still use fails loudly instead of silently repointing them.

One ingredient must not be offered by two slots of the SAME composite: resolveOrder maps ingredient to slot per composite with the last write winning, so a dish authored into one slot silently resolves into the other, carrying a gate that can never open. Sharing an ingredient across two DIFFERENT orderables is allowed — a bracket dish names its composite, so lookup is scoped to it. That case was once an error ("C2") only because the retired legacy flat-list recogniser could not tell the composites apart.

Every member of a dish belongs to the composite its outermost bracket names. The bracket format makes the shape single-orderable by construction; this catches a member smuggled into a bracket it does not belong to, e.g. a soda cup inside a burger.
At most one process edge targets any ingredient. An ingredient with no producer must be pickupable.
No cycles in process/base/topping/option edges.
Vertex names are unique across ALL kinds — base/topping/option edges resolve into one shared namespace.
Every distinct leaf reachable from an orderable composite bottoms out at a pickupable ingredient.
Every composite has exactly one base edge.
A group's minQuantity is non-negative and cannot exceed a finite maxQuantity.
A dirty node's optional maxStack must be a positive integer.
Every group has at least one option edge.
A composite marked toppingRequired actually has a topping edge to require. Marking it without one makes every order of that composite unfillable.
An ingredient produced by a tool but consumed by nothing and not reachable from any orderable.
A pickupable ingredient no orderable reaches.
A composite no orderable reaches.
An orderable's concrete-variant count is unbounded because a MULTIPLE group on its path is uncapped. Expected for build-your-own items; stated so it is a choice, not an accident.
A tool with no process edges.
A group with exactly one option and no room for repeats — the choice is not a choice.
A pickupable or order-slot ingredient — or an orderable composite, or a group reachable from one — with no id-table entry. It cannot be referenced by level data until an id is minted.
A process edge with more than one input. The data keeps the list, but the v1 simulation reads only inputs[0].
Every process input's `slot` indexes a real entry of the source tool's slotConfigs. An out-of-range point can never be filled, so the recipe would silently never run.

One ingredient always enters a given tool at the same point, across every recipe of that tool. Dispatch routes an incoming pickup by ingredient, so two recipes disagreeing about where it goes makes the destination undecidable.
A multi-input recipe whose points have different lane counts. Only the shared lanes can ever pair up; the surplus lanes of the wider point can be filled but never completed.
